newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end flat after seesaw session.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end flat after seesaw session.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended flat on Friday after the market benchmark wandered in both negative and positive ranges for most of the day.

"Thursday's property-related share rally spilled over into the Friday session while a stronger yen prompted profit-taking of export-strong blue-chip shares, forcing the Nikkei average to seesaw around the 19,000 level," said Akihiro Naemura, general manager at Okasan Securities.
The Nikkei 225 clawed back above the 19,000 line to close down 17.17 points or 0.09 percent at 19,034.54. Its March futures were down 40 points at 19,030.
Brokers said the Nikkei 225 and its futures were weighed down by selling of recent high flyers such as Sony Corp, which shed 140 yen to end at 8,750.

But the TOPIX index, encompassing banking, construction and other sectors groaning under bad loans, kept climbing, still nourished by newspaper reports on Thursday that the government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan firms and other troubled financial institutions.
The TOPIX rose 13.35 points or 0.95 percent to end at 1,425.01. The Nikkei 300 added 2.97 points or 1.10 percent to close at 273.90.
